Airbus SE Reports Strong Quarterly Earnings Amid Steady Aircraft Deliveries

AMSTERDAM, June 20 — Airbus SE reported a rise in quarterly earnings on Thursday, buoyed by continued strong demand for commercial aircraft and robust performance in its defense and space division.

The Netherlands-based aerospace manufacturer said adjusted earnings before interest and tax rose 8% to €1.7 billion for the first quarter, up from €1.58 billion a year earlier. Revenue climbed 6% to €12.9 billion, supported by higher deliveries of its A320neo family of aircraft and increased activity in its helicopter business.

“Our teams have delivered a solid set of results, reflecting the resilience of our business model and the continued confidence of our customers,” Chief Executive Guillaume Faury said in a statement. “We are on track to meet our full-year targets, with a strong order book and a robust outlook for both commercial and defense markets.”

Airbus delivered 142 commercial aircraft during the quarter, compared with 125 in the same period last year. The company said it continued to see “healthy demand” from airlines seeking newer, more fuel-efficient jets in the wake of sustained passenger traffic growth.

The company’s defense and space division reported sales growth of 4%, with several new contracts signed with European and Middle Eastern governments. “We are seeing stable demand in the defense sector, bolstered by investments in modernizing fleets and strengthening national capabilities,” said Chief Financial Officer Thomas van der Meer.

Analysts welcomed the results, citing Airbus’ ability to navigate ongoing supply chain pressures and global economic uncertainties. “Airbus continues to demonstrate operational discipline and adaptability,” said Marieke Jansen, aerospace sector analyst at Rotterdam-based brokerage Van Dijk Partners. “The positive momentum in commercial aircraft is particularly encouraging, given the competitive landscape.”

Airbus reaffirmed its guidance for the year, targeting around 720 commercial aircraft deliveries and an adjusted EBIT of €6 billion. The company said it remains focused on ramping up production of its best-selling narrow-body jets and investing in new technologies aimed at reducing emissions.

Shares in Airbus SE rose 2.3% in early Amsterdam trading following the announcement.

The company, which employs over 130,000 people worldwide, maintains major operations in France, Germany, Spain, and the United Kingdom, in addition to its Dutch headquarters. The Netherlands Aerospace Association noted that Airbus’ performance “underscores the importance of the aerospace sector to the national and European economies.”
